title: Majestic: The Bishop Blocks Its Own Rook
summary: Promote with check when a capturing bishop interrupts its own rook’s defense, then finish the king cage with the queen.

nodes.question: Why can the c-pawn promote while a rook still stands on c1?
nodes.explanation: The black bishop on c4 blocks Rc1’s path to c8. White can promote with check, forcing the king into a short queen mating net.

branches.title: Source finish after the bishop captures
commentary: Begin after ...Bxc4 in this source variation. All three black pawns, Rc1, Bc4 and White’s g7 pawn remain on the board.
c8=Q+ promotes with a diagonal check against Ka6. Rc1 cannot capture the new queen because its own bishop on c4 blocks the file.
Kb6 is forced: Kb8 controls a7 and b7, the new queen checks a6 and covers c6, and Black’s a5/b5 pawns occupy other flights.
Qc7+ checks along the seventh-rank diagonal to b6 and keeps the king boxed against its own pawns.
Ka6 is the sole legal reply. The queen controls c6 and c5, while the white king controls b7.
Qa7# checks down the a-file. Kb8 protects a7 and b7, the queen controls b6, and Black’s own a5/b5 pawns close the remaining escape squares.

exercises.answer: The black bishop on c4 blocks the rook’s path up the c-file.
White’s king on b8 controls a7, so the black king cannot capture the checking queen.
